chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: Singers: Duke Groner, Herb Jeffries, Ida James
summary: Always a male and female singer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Duke Gro\ner was signing with Horace at some time around there. Do you know Duke?
Yeah, I know Duke well. I met Duke in Omaha. He was just singing then. He wasn't even playing bass.
And -- or he might have stayed here after Horace -- no, I think he went to New York. But anyway, he got back to Chicago some way and started playing
bass.
Yeah.
He still sings good.
Yes, he does.
I love the way Duke sings. Not many guys sing like that.
Speaking of singers, where did Herb Jeffries come from?
Picked him up in Washington, D. C., too.
Really?
Yeah.
He sounded an awful lot like Bing Crosby on those early records. Much different than when he was with Duke.
Yeah.
Well, you know we talked earlier about the band having regular vocalists. And you talked about Herb and Billy Eckstine. And there was -- were there girl singers, too?
Yes. Outside of Valaida Snow we had Ida James, and what was her name? Last name was Washington, I'm trying to think of her first name. She's real tall girl. We picked her up in Washington.
But there was always a male and a female singer?
Always a male and a female.
And they sat on the bandstand, clapped their hands, and all that stuff?
Yeah.
Were they featured in the show? Did they have a spot in the show?
They had a spot in the show, too, yeah. We had another male vocalist that was very good, too, nicknamed "Georgia Boy."
What was his real --
Can't think of it. Can't think of it. His nickname was Georgia Boy. That's all we used, was Georgia Boy, you know, in advertising.
